deep.reconstruction:
The page holds only two handwritten lines, and the whole passage is struck through with long diagonal strokes. Reading the image: "On a ainsi la notion de graphe pseudo-[uni?]cellulaire (fournie par Γ/Σ, la structure ..." ("We thus have the notion of a pseudo-(uni?)cellular graph (provided by Γ/Σ, the structure ..."). The sentence breaks off.

Context:
- The previous page (43) sets up topological Teichmüller groupoids. Its objects are compact oriented surfaces with boundary; its arrows are isotopy classes of homeomorphisms. It introduces the orientation-forgetting variant and the signature map to [±1]. It announces the 'special decorated' variant S_*TD_top.
- The next page (45) restarts that definition cleanly. Objects are triples (X, Σ̃, R): Σ̃ = ∂X ⨿ Σ, where Σ is a family of cutting circles, and R is a finite set of rigidification points. It then lists full subgroupoids and mentions Mumford–Deligne. It begins determining π_0 of S_*TD_top via 'bi-weighted graphs' (graphes bipondérés).

The abandoned sentence therefore seems to be a first attempt to attach a combinatorial graph to a decorated surface, as the invariant classifying isotopy/homeomorphism classes.
- In modern terms this is the dual graph of a multicurve decomposition: vertices are the components of X cut along Σ, edges are the cutting circles, and vertices carry genus and puncture/boundary data.
- This is the topological counterpart of the stable graphs that index the boundary strata of the Deligne–Mumford compactification.
- 'Pseudo-cellular' may instead refer to the cell-complement structure of a graph embedded in a surface (a map, in the sense of dessins d'enfants).

Grothendieck abandoned the formulation and replaced it on p.45 with the bi-weighted graph approach. The underlying problem is classifying objects of the decorated Teichmüller groupoid up to isomorphism, i.e. computing π_0.
